Every card payment in India ends the same way: you wait for a code.


The OTP is the last human step in a card transaction. It exists to prove a person is really there at the moment of purchase. Which is fine, until the person doing the shopping isn’t a person at all.


Over the last two years, AI agents have quietly taken over the top of the funnel. Customers describe what they want, and the agent compares, shortlists, and decides. But when it comes time to actually pay by card, the agent hits a wall it was never going to clear: a one-time password sent to someone’s phone, waiting for the authorization.


At GFF 2026, Cashfree has launched Agentic Payments on RAP, RuPay’s framework for letting an AI agent pay by card on a customer’s behalf. Instead of asking for approval at every checkout, it takes it once, up front, and lets the agent carry that permission forward.


Here’s how that works, and why it changes things.


##


**An agentic card payment, defined**


An agentic card payment is a purchase an AI agent completes with your RuPay card, carrying cryptographic proof that you authorised it.


The proof is the whole point. The agent is never improvising with your card. It acts inside a permission you granted, and every purchase is checked against that permission before any money moves. If the agent tries to spend beyond what you allowed, or somewhere you didn’t approve, the payment fails on its own.


Take a customer who tells their agent once: *“Book Bengaluru to Delhi if the fare drops below ₹5,000.”* Two weeks later it touches ₹4,700 at 6 in the morning. The agent checks the rule, books the seat, and pays with the card the customer assigned. No one woke up. No OTP was typed. And at no point did the agent actually see the card.


##


**The new idea: A token that belongs to your agent**


To pull that off, RAP introduces something cards haven’t had before: a token tied to an *agent* .


Until now, a saved card token was tied to a merchant. Your card-on-file at one store didn’t work at another. RAP flips the axis. When you link your RuPay card to an AI agent, RuPay issues a token bound to you and to that specific agent, and it works across any merchant the agent shops at. The real card number is never handed to the AI platform. The token is non-transferable, and you can pull it back in a single tap whenever you want.


Around that token sit two guardrails that make it safe to hand an agent spending power:


**Only known agents can hold one.** Every agent is registered and cryptographically identifiable before it can transact, so a payment always traces back to a specific agent tied to a specific customer.


**Every payment carries its own rulebook.** Each transaction ships with a signed cart and a reference to the policy you set, your spending cap, the categories you allowed, how long the permission lasts. Miss any of it, or breach it, and the payment doesn’t go through.


RuPay keeps the registry of all of it, the signed carts, the policies, and a full audit trail for every agentic transaction, which is also what makes disputes and chargebacks work the way customers expect.


**Two modes, one question: when do you tap?**


The difference between RAP’s two modes is simply where the human approval lands.


**Authorised, the tap happens every time.** The agent builds the cart, and you approve each purchase with an OTP or a biometric passkey on your bank’s secure page. You’re present for every payment. It’s the checkout you know today, just living inside the chat instead of a browser tab.


**Autonomous, the tap happens once.** You set the rules and authenticate a single time, up front. After that, the agent buys within those bounds while you’re away, no fresh approval per purchase. This is what lets the 6 a.m. flight booking happen without you.


Both are card payments. The only thing that changes is whether you’re in the room when they run.

##


**What a business has to do**


For all the machinery underneath, the lift for a merchant is small.


**Expose one MCP server.** A standard Model Context Protocol interface lets agents browse your catalogue, check price and stock, and build a cart. One server works across ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and every platform that onboards after them. This is what puts your products in front of an agent at all.


**Add a small delta to your card flow.** Your existing Cashfree card acceptance stays put. Agentic transactions simply carry a few extra fields marking them as agent-originated, and Cashfree handles the token work and verification beneath. It’s additive, not a re-platforming.


The payoff is the drop-off you lose today. The customer who has already decided, and then evaporates somewhere between the cart and the code, is exactly the customer this keeps.


##


**Where it goes first**


Some flows only become possible once the consent is standardised and RuPay backed:


**Wait-for-the-price purchases.** An agent watching a fare, a flash sale, or a restock inside a budget you approved can buy the instant conditions are met. No human-in-the-loop checkout can move that fast, which is why travel and other wait-for-the-right-price categories are the natural first home for card agentic payments.


**Checkout that never leaves the chat.** A customer asks, the agent buys, and it’s done in the same conversation, on the catalogue and pricing you already publish.


**Hands-off replenishment.** Sign a policy once for the things you rebuy, and the agent reorders against it, no repeat approval, useful for the subscription-shaped purchases that never had a formal subscription.


**Standing wishlists.** Items an agent is holding convert the moment price or stock matches the intent you left with it.


**One intent across many merchants.** A single approved intent can span several sellers, so “plan and book this weekend” can play out across a few merchants under one consent.


##


**Where Cashfree fits in**


This is less a RuPay story than an infrastructure one, and it’s where Cashfree lives.


RAP rests on a layered chain of responsibility: the regulated **agency** that creates agents, the individual **agent** tied to a customer or a merchant, and the signed **action** every payment must point to. Cashfree carries trust across that whole chain, from the agent down to the actual debit.


On the customer’s side, Cashfree is the piece that links a RuPay card to an AI platform: it collects the card in a secure frame the platform never sees, runs the authentication, mints the agent token, and registers the agent with RuPay. Cashfree’s token vault and authentication switch are what make this possible.


On the merchant’s side, Cashfree helps a business stand up as an agent, checks the signed cart against the registry before a payment runs, translates the token so the merchant is paid on its own credentials, and carries the transaction through to settlement.


Net for a merchant: agentic card commerce without a second integration, a second compliance surface, or a second settlement system. And when the agent becomes the buyer, you collect at the peak of intent, instead of losing that customer to a code they never typed.
